newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar maintains overnight gains vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar maintains overnight gains vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: 0311 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT

The dollar maintained its overnight gains and stayed above 114 yen by midday Tokyo on Friday after worries over U.S.-Japan trade friction receded in the wake of comments by President Bill Clinton, dealers said.
The market is waiting for the outcome of the Group of Seven (G7) nations' summit this weekend, but some dealers say the market's focus may shift to Japan's "tankan" survey next week.

In a White House interview recorded for Japanese television before departing for the Denver summit on Thursday, Clinton said he was concerned about Japan's large surplus with the United States but added that exchange rates should not be used as a way to correct trade imbalances.
Dealers said the tone of his comments was not as strong as the market had anticipated and this led to short-covering.

Clinton also voiced concern about Japan's trade surplus in a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutoro Hashimoto on Thursday in Denver, but dealers said the impact was limited as he made similar comments previously.
"Trade remains directionless as traders are still nervous ahead of the summit," a city bank dealer said.
But some dealers said the market may shift its focus to the results of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) key quarterly "tankan" corporate survey due to be released on June 25.

"I don't think the issue of Japan's trade surplus will be discussed intensively at the summit," a city bank dealer said, adding that dealers have begun to pay less attention to U.S.-Japan trade issues now they have seen Clinton's comments.
Dealers said U.S. funds and Japanese trust banks were major buyers of the greenback for yen in morning trade.
The dollar rose as high as 114.68 yen in early trade after stop-loss purchases were triggered near 114.55 yen, a dealer at an Australian bank said.
A city bank dealer said U.S. funds were also buying marks and Swiss francs for yen in cross trade, which indirectly helped buoy the dollar/yen rate.
The mark stood near 66.42/45 yen at 0344 GMT, compared with 66.17 yen in late New York trade on Thursday, while the Swiss franc was at 79.59/64 yen, up from 79.30 yen in New York.
But a slew of exporters offers was lined up near 114.70 yen and above, capping the dollar's gains, dealers said.
The city bank dealer also said some options-linked dollar offers may be placed by U.S. operators near 115.50 yen.
The dollar received a boost against the yen on short-covering in New York on Thursday after the U.S. Commerce Department reported a smaller-than-expected U.S. trade deficit in April.
The trade gap was $8.36 billion, well below the $10 billion shortfall priced into the market but still larger than the downwardly-revised $7.76 billion in March.
The dollar ended at 114.60/11 yen and 1.7235/45 marks in New York. - Yoko Nishikawa, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8584
